phase_title: Non-Unix Durability, Runtime-wide Deadline, and MCP Crash-Window Evidence
scope: local Runtime durable task-state write ordering
local and Windows atomic write file fsync and parent directory sync behavior
MCP stdio process-local monotonic deadline accounting across response wait and child-exit wait
task terminal mutation lock, freshness checks, and terminal state/ledger transition recovery
durable write failure injection for disk-full, rename denial, and truncated temporary state

source_checks.requirement: TaskStore::write_task_state uses write_file_atomically instead of raw fs::write plus fs::rename.

write_file_atomically creates a sibling temporary file with create_new, writes and fsyncs the file, rejects symlink/reparse durable targets, atomically replaces the destination, and syncs the parent directory.
RunLedger::append_many fsyncs appended terminal evidence and syncs the run directory before terminal transition markers are removed.
McpStdioDeadline carries a process-local monotonic expiration instant and reconstructs remaining timeout budget instead of resetting the budget between stdio response wait and child-exit wait.
stdio_request waits for the MCP child to exit only until the remaining McpStdioDeadline and then records process-tree kill evidence on timeout.
MCP stdio subprocesses run in their own Unix process group, timeout handling terminates the process tree, and timeout errors expose bounded process-tree cleanup evidence.
Runtime tests cover MCP stdio timeout cleanup and approval timeout terminalization without approval reuse.

Task terminal status updates acquire a per-run terminal-mutation lock, re-read latest state inside the lock, and require expected current status plus updated_at freshness before terminal completion or cancellation evidence.
Terminal status transitions persist terminal-transition.json before state mutation, append a prebuilt terminal ledger event, and recover a state-written/ledger-missing process-loss window on restart.
Test-only durable write failpoints cover disk_full_before_write, truncated_state_before_rename, and rename_denied_after_sync without replacing committed state or leaking temporary files.

Windows durable writes use MoveFileExW with replace/write-through flags, reject reparse-point targets, and sync parent directories through FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS; unsupported non-Unix/non-Windows directory sync and atomic replace fail closed.
Windows stale process-lock recovery uses OpenProcess and zero-time WaitForSingleObject liveness checks before atomically claiming and removing dead-owner lock files.

task.run accepts a bounded RuntimeDeadline, persists it into TaskRecord while transitioning to Running, rejects deadline mismatches on resume, and fails closed before resume mutation when the persisted wall-clock deadline has expired.
A test-only child-process abort after MCP ToolExecutionCompleted and before terminal task recording proves restart/recovery has durable tool completion evidence for the remaining MCP crash window.

closure.implemented_scope: RRP-7.2 closes the remaining platform/deadline/durability release blocker by adding Windows durability and stale-lock recovery behavior, fail-closed unsupported-platform durability boundaries, Runtime-wide persisted deadline propagation with resume-time expiry checks, and MCP response-after-receive crash-window process-loss evidence.
closure.summary: RRP-7.2 builds on RRP-7.1's local Unix MCP stdio deadline, terminal mutation lock, terminal-transition marker, and durable write failpoint evidence. The Runtime/store now rejects symlink and Windows reparse durable targets before atomic replacement, uses Windows MoveFileExW write-through replacement and directory sync where available, fails closed for unsupported non-Unix/non-Windows durable primitives, reclaims dead-owner process locks on Windows by checking process liveness, persists caller-supplied task/run deadlines in TaskRecord, rejects resume deadline mismatches, terminalizes non-terminal tasks that are resumed after an expired deadline, and proves the MCP tool-completed/terminal-task-not-yet-recorded process-loss window with a real child-process abort test.
